speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with rectal bleeding and a palpable rectal mass; please describe the color of the blood (bright red or dark), how much is bleeding, and how long this has been occurring. Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as narrowing of the stool or a feeling of incomplete evacuation?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Colorectal Cancer.

Based on your 2-week history of painless rectal bleeding and the presence of a palpable rectal mass, I strongly suspect a malignancy. I am requesting an immediate Colonoscopy with biopsy and a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to confirm the diagnosis and stage the disease.
